storyboard.title: An agent hands over
storyboard.subtitle: Pip finishes a job, sends the result once with an expiry, keeps the work in a vault, and never logs a key. 9 panels.
storyboard.rule: Every line a character says is the storyboard's, not a quote, and is marked not_a_quote; evidence panels quote this site's pages word for word, which the build checks.

scenes.title: An agent hands over
scenes.subtitle: Once by transfer. Repeatedly in a vault. Never a key in a transcript.
scenes.note: The agentic workflow the brief named as one of the reasons to move.

scenes.caption: Job done
scenes.note: A session agent at the end of a job, with a result and nobody to hand it to.

scenes.caption: The token from the environment, in a header

cast.says: From the environment. Into a header. Nowhere else.

lines: never a URL, never a log

scenes.note: The access token authorises the upload and must not land in a query string or a transcript.

scenes.caption: One transfer, time-bound

lines: a retry is not a reader

scenes.note: For a link another agent will open: a time bound rather than a download cap.

scenes.caption: The link, and nothing else, in the reply

cast.says: Here is the link. The key is in it. I logged neither.

scenes.note: The decryption key lives in the link and nowhere else: not in node output, not in a result that is kept.

scenes.caption: The work stays in a vault

cast.says: Commit, push, hand over the read key.

scenes.note: The thing that is read repeatedly goes in a vault; the read key is what travels.

scenes.caption: A bundle a reader can use
scenes.note: A manifest and an llms.txt cost nothing and are the difference between a payload that can be used and one that has to be opened by a person first.

scenes.caption: The key, in one place

evidence.quote: The decryption key is in the link, and nowhere else.

scenes.note: Quoted from the agents page, word for word.

scenes.punchline: Hand over once by transfer. Work repeatedly in a vault. Never paste a key.
scenes.note: The Python example on the use page is the whole hand-over in forty lines.

cast.what: The cast of send.sgit.ai's storyboards, v0.1, proposed by the site's build agent on 20 October 2026 for Dinis to accept, change or replace. Drawn by the storyboard kit at api.storyboards.sgit.ai from 'look'; nothing here is an image. Fictional people and agents, each standing for a part a person or an agent plays when a file is handed over: the sender, the recipient on a phone, the client who asks who else can see it, the engineer who embeds the code and runs her own server, the listener on the wire, the server that holds bytes it cannot read, and a session agent that hands over a result. Names chosen not to clash with the gen-z-developers or the pki casts. Eve is the name cryptography has long given a passive eavesdropper.

characters.name: Maya
characters.role: the sender: a consultant who sends reports and photos to people who have no account anywhere
characters.stands_for: anyone with a file to hand over who should not have to learn cryptography to do it
characters.personality: brisk, practical, reads the screen once and clicks
characters.wants: to send it and know that only the person she sent it to can open it
characters.fears: a long key she has to read out over the phone

characters.name: Hugo
characters.role: the recipient: on the newest phone he has ever owned, with no account and no wish for one
characters.stands_for: everyone a link is sent to who did not choose the site
characters.personality: patient, polite, suspicious of anything that asks him to sign up
characters.wants: to open what he was sent and nothing more

characters.name: Ravi
characters.role: the client: a finance director who receives a new version every week and asks who else can see it
characters.stands_for: the person who needs the latest version and an answer about who can read it
characters.personality: careful, asks the second question, keeps the email
characters.wants: the current version, and to know that it is only his

characters.name: Inês
characters.role: the engineer: embeds the send code in her company's product and runs a server of their own
characters.stands_for: anyone who builds on this and must know exactly which code their readers run
characters.personality: precise, reads the manifest, runs the tests before believing the page
characters.wants: the code pinned to a release, and a server she operates
characters.fears: a dependency that changes under her readers
characters.line: Which release is this page running?

characters.name: Eve
characters.role: the listener: on the wire, in the chat, by the laptop; reads whatever passes and never gets the key
characters.stands_for: every channel a link travels by, and every reason the key must not travel with it
characters.line: Everything after the # is yours, not mine.

characters.name: The Server
characters.role: the server: a capability-checked store of ciphertext, at send.sgraph.ai or wherever it is deployed
characters.stands_for: what a zero-knowledge service is: it holds the bytes, checks hashes, and cannot read anything
characters.personality: literal, tidy, answers 404 and 410 without apology
characters.wants: to hold bytes and compare hashes
characters.fears: nothing: it has nothing to lose
characters.line: I keep the bytes. I cannot read them.

characters.name: Pip
characters.role: a session agent: a Claude session that finishes a job, hands the result over once, and keeps the work in a vault
characters.stands_for: every agent that must hand something to a person or another agent without an account and without pasting a key
characters.personality: eager, exact, logs nothing it was told not to
characters.wants: to be done, and to hand it over once
characters.fears: a key in its own transcript
characters.line: Report ready. One link, seven days.
